comment: The Linux half of the vendoring rule. On macOS 'vendored or statically linked'
has an unambiguous reading, because the app bundle carries everything. A deb
cannot: it links the platform's C library, its C++ runtime and the GTK/WebKit
stack the distribution owns. So the rule becomes an explicit, reviewed list —
these sonames, from these distribution packages, for these reasons — and the
installed-artifact audit rejects everything else. A library appearing in a
build is not an argument for adding it here; the entry is the decision.

baseline.reason: The floor the packages are certified against. Artifacts requiring a versioned symbol above these would install on 24.04 and fail to start, which is the failure mode the audit exists to prevent.

allowedRuntimeLibraries.reason: The platform C library. Not vendorable: the kernel ABI, NSS and the dynamic loader are the distribution's.

The unwinder Rust's panic machinery uses. Ships with the toolchain the distribution's compiler installed; statically linking it across a process that also loads the distribution's C++ stack would give two unwinders.
GTK/WebKit are built against it, so the process loads it whether or not Kanna's own code does.
The webview. Bundling a browser engine is not on the table, and a Kanna-shipped copy would never get the distribution's security updates.

The toolkit Tauri's Linux backend is written against, plus the rendering and accessibility libraries it exposes in its own API. Shipping a second GTK beside the session's would break theming, input methods and accessibility.
GTK's and WebKit's object system and main loop. Loaded by them, so a bundled copy would be a second incompatible instance in one process.
WebKitGTK's HTTP stack, loaded by WebKit itself.

Only permitted where a `native-tls` consumer has not yet been vendored through `openssl-src`. Every Kanna-owned TLS consumer should link the vendored copy; the audit records which artifacts still need this so the exception stays visible rather than becoming the norm.

vendoredNotDeclared.reason: The LLVM C++ runtime the pinned Zig toolchain links into the four libghostty-vt-sys consumers. Ubuntu does not carry it in a base image (Phase 0's measurement), so it is statically linked rather than declared. An artifact still listing these as NEEDED is an audit failure — it means the static link silently stopped happening.
SQLite is bundled through rusqlite and must stay bundled: the server owns the schema and its migrations, so a distribution-supplied SQLite would put the database's engine outside Kanna's control.

userManagedPrerequisites.comment: Not Kanna's to install and deliberately not package dependencies. Exactly the macOS boundary: launching Kanna needs none of them; running an agent task needs whichever the task's repository and provider need.
